article.title: NFL EDGE Sunday Morning Brief
article.dek: Game day brings a new Minnesota recommendation, a much cheaper Kansas City price, and injury and weather decisions across the full Sunday slate.

items.headline: Quarterbacks and weather headline the Sunday board
paragraphs: Minnesota will start Carson Wentz at Chicago with Kyler Murray out, while Seattle will start Drew Lock at Arizona with Sam Darnold out. Atlanta is also dealing with a major quarterback situation: Michael Penix Jr. is out and Tua Tagovailoa is doubtful, leaving Cooper Rush set to start. Baltimore receiver Zay Flowers is doubtful, Raiders tight end Brock Bowers is doubtful, and Houston receiver Nico Collins remains out against Cincinnati.

Weather is worth a final check in several outdoor games. Vikings-Bears has rain in the forecast, Packers-Jets is expected to be wet, rain chances build during Steelers-Patriots and Saints-Ravens, and Colts-Chiefs still carries a meaningful rain risk Sunday night. Eagles-Titans is the opposite problem: Nashville is expected to be extremely hot.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: Game-day information finally moved the card
paragraphs: Minnesota is now one of the headline plays at +4.5, so the Wentz start and Chicago weather deserve attention before kickoff. Cincinnati is still on the card at +2.5, with Houston missing Collins. Kansas City remains the moneyline play for Sunday night, but the price has improved enough to matter.

The rest of the app still matters too. Seattle-Arizona, Atlanta-Carolina, Baltimore-New Orleans and the wet outdoor games all have meaningful game-day context that should be checked against the live matchup view rather than ignored because they are not headline bets.

items.headline: Kansas City is popular, but the line is moving the other way
paragraphs: Kansas City is drawing the crowd Sunday night. Action Network's current board shows roughly 78% of spread bets on the Chiefs, yet the market has moved from Kansas City -6.5 to around -5.5. That's the disagreement worth watching: bettors are piling onto Kansas City while the spread has become a little easier for Chiefs backers rather than more expensive.

That does not automatically mean the Colts are the right side, and NFL EDGE's recommendation is the Kansas City moneyline rather than the spread. But it is a good reason not to chase the Chiefs if the moneyline gets worse before kickoff.
items.takeaway: Kansas City remains playable at the NFL EDGE-approved moneyline through -259. If that price disappears, wait rather than following the crowd at a worse number. If the spread keeps moving toward Indianapolis while Chiefs betting stays heavily concentrated, that disagreement becomes even more meaningful.

items.headline: Minnesota arrives, Cincinnati changes roles, and Kansas City gets much cheaper
paragraphs: Minnesota +4.5 at -102 is the new spread headline this morning, playable through -105. Cincinnati +2.5 at -102 is still recommended through -105, but it is now the value play rather than the primary spread headline.

Kansas City remains the moneyline recommendation, and this is the biggest price improvement of the morning: DraftKings is now -250, playable through -259. The recommended stake also rises to 0.75 units. Last night the best approved Chiefs price was FanDuel -280, so this is a materially better deal on the same team.
items.takeaway: Use the Sunday-morning card, not Saturday night's screenshot. Minnesota is new, Cincinnati is still alive in a different role, and Kansas City is substantially cheaper at DraftKings.

items.headline: Game day is when stale screenshots get expensive
paragraphs: A bet you saved last night may not be the bet NFL EDGE wants this morning. Books change, prices move and recommendations can rotate as new information arrives. Before placing anything on Sunday, reopen the current card and verify the team, sportsbook, line, price and Play Through. Thirty seconds of checking can keep you from betting yesterday's version of today's game.
